name: The deployment shock
thesis: AI agents take over knowledge work faster than institutions can absorb it. Politics catches up through crisis rather than foresight.
life: Your job changes before your title does: the work is set up for an agent and you check it. New graduates feel it first. Everything digital gets cheaper and more suspect at once.
uncertainty: Whether institutions respond to the first big incident with rules or with panic.

name: The restructuring
thesis: The singularity question gets answered in a form nobody finds satisfying, and the hinge resolves one way or the other.
life: Fewer paid hours, more arguments about who pays. The first drugs and robots that were obviously designed by machines arrive. Someone you know works beside a system that is better than anyone at the job.
uncertainty: The hinge: whether the most capable systems stay in many hands or a few.

name: The divergence
thesis: Population peaks, aging is slowed, 2°C is breached, and governance of superhuman systems settles into a regime, legitimate or not.
bad: The nation-state loses ground to firms and city-regions
life: Where you live decides more than what you earn. Aging slows for those who can get the therapy. The weather is the thing the news argues about.
uncertainty: Whether governance of superhuman systems is legitimate, or merely effective.

name: The slow world and the fast world
thesis: Population declines. Abundance for the well-governed; surveillance or disorder for the rest.
bad: Humans mostly out of the decision loop
life: Long lives, small families, and a world that runs mostly without human labor. Whether that feels like freedom or like being managed depends on the institutions you were born under.
uncertainty: How far population falls, and whether the well-governed places stay open to the rest.

name: The sketch
thesis: Humans and AI either merge into something continuous, or humans persist as a protected, long-lived population beside the systems that do the civilizational work.
bad: Permanent loss of control remains a ~5% tail
life: A sketch, not a forecast: humans either continuous with their systems or kept beside them. Either way, most of what matters is decided by minds that are not human.
uncertainty: Whether 'human' still names a boundary anyone cares to defend.
